","groupId":"97a97645-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"About the Major","groupId":"b0207745-6887-ef11-8474-000d3a37e3b6","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

The mission of the CSUB Department of Art and Art History is to advance creative research and critical thinking while fostering an encouraging environment for cultural inquiry and artistic experimentation. Located at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley, the Art and Gallery Programs complement the University’s larger mission by offering CSUB students an opportunity to engage in advanced critical discourse both local and international in scope. The Art Program has a strong local presence but is also designed, in part, to expose the campus and community to the visual culture and sociopolitical currents present in the Los Angeles region and the larger San Joaquin Valley. The Zaninovich Visiting Artist Lecture Series welcomes four prominent speakers each semester to address a wide range of contemporary creative, social, and cultural issues. Each academic year the Todd Madigan Visiting Artist Program invites an established contemporary artist to work directly with students in building a gallery exhibition, while the Sculptors on Campus Program invites an established public artist to work directly with students in building an public art installation on the CSUB campus. Our distinguished Art and Art History faculty is comprised of nine full-time practicing artists, art historians, and art educators, complemented by an accomplished roster of lecturers and three full-time staff, serving over 125 Art majors as well as the university and community as a whole. The department maintains state-of-the-art facilities for Ceramics, Sculpture, Painting, Drawing, Printmaking, Photography, and Digital Media, as well as senior studio spaces.


For additional information, visit the following:

Department of Art and Art History
